additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is characterized by a continuous period of illness during which there is a major depressive episode concurrent with symptoms of schizophrenia, such as delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized thinking. To meet criteria, there must also be at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms without prominent mood symptoms, distinguishing it from mood disorders with psychotic features. The course is typically chronic or episodic, with variable functional impairment in work, relationships, and self‑care, and it often emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood. Compared with schizophrenia, mood symptoms are more prominent and recurrent, while compared with major depressive disorder with psychotic features, psychotic symptoms are more enduring and not strictly limited to mood episodes.

patient.stressor: Jessie’s current episode took shape over the past couple of years, coinciding with the final breakdown of her marriage and the practical realities of living alone in Lancaster after the divorce. At first she threw herself into work as a crossing guard and community events—choir rehearsals, block parties, youth basketball coaching—as a way to stay busy and surrounded by people, but friends noticed that her usual lively disorganization turned into missed rehearsals, unreturned calls, and last‑minute cancellations. Over roughly eighteen months, the strain of managing her home, finances, and social commitments without a partner, along with ongoing tension with her ex‑spouse about family gatherings, wore down her usual resilience, and she began skipping gardening club meetings and church events that once anchored her week. Her adult daughter finally persuaded her to seek psychiatric help after Jessie admitted during a Sunday dinner that she’d been feeling like a burden to everyone and had been pulling back from the community because she “wasn’t sure [she] deserved to be around folks anymore.”
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t shake this feeling that I’m a burden to everyone around me and that I’ve let my whole community down.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For a long time now I’ve been convinced that some of the parents and even the city people are secretly keeping tabs on me—like when they stand a little too long near the corner where I work or I get a letter from the school district, I’m sure they’re documenting my mistakes so they can prove I’m unfit to be around the kids.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: Pretty much every week I hear this man’s voice, kind of behind my left ear, commenting on what I’m doing—telling me I’m useless or that the kids would be safer if I wasn’t there—even when I’m alone in my apartment with the TV off and I know no one else is around.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: These days it feels like the light just went out in me—I stand at my post, do the bare minimum at home, and when my daughter or church friends invite me out I just stare at the phone because I can’t bring myself to care enough to say yes or even text back.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like there’s no point to getting out of bed, and even when I make it to the crosswalk I feel like I’m just going through the motions with this gray cloud sitting on me that never really lifts.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Over the past year I’ve mostly had to force myself to eat because food just doesn’t appeal to me anymore—I’ll go all day on coffee and maybe a cracker, and then realize my pants are getting loose but still have no interest in fixing an actual meal.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: My body feels like it’s moving through mud, so I shuffle across the street slower than I used to, and when someone asks me a simple question, like what time my shift ends, it can take me a few long seconds just to get the words out.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I walk past the school and feel this crushing sense that I’ve failed everyone—my ex, my daughter, the kids, the choir—like I’m some kind of rotten core in the middle of the community, and any little problem that happens, from a near-miss with a car to a low turnout at a church event, I’m sure it’s somehow my fault and that I ought to step aside so people can be better off without me.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: Lately my mind feels foggy all the time—I'll read the same note from the school three or four times and still can’t hold onto what it said, and even picking between two shirts in the morning can take me ten minutes because I just can’t think straight enough to decide.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: For months I’ve caught myself thinking it would be easier for everyone if I just didn’t wake up, and on my worst days I picture stepping off the curb in front of one of the trucks when the light changes, enough that I sometimes have to grip the stop sign pole to keep from getting too close to the street.
